title: space-bearing names — source file + vault file whose basenames contain spaces, matching ledger row
spec_case: V8: vault file + source file whose names contain spaces. Expected: VERIFIED.
intent: A fake vault file and a source file whose basenames BOTH contain literal spaces (and are deliberately different names, the shape a real export produces: source `meeting notes 2026-10.md` -> vault `Meeting Notes 2026-10.md`). A ledger row in tests/vault/ledger-V8.tsv matches source path + source sha256 + vault path + vault sha256 (all four conjuncts, both path fields carrying literal spaces). Expected verdict: VERIFIED (receipt moved-to-obsidian).
path_convention: substitute @FIXTURE_ROOT@ with the FIXTURE_ROOT printed by make-fixture.sh; make-fixture.sh also writes the substituted copy to <ROOT>/expected.json. Evaluate the target by that exact absolute path — ledger matching is path-exact and the path contains spaces, so it must be quoted in every shell use.
ledger_header: source_path	source_sha256	vault_path	vault_sha256	exported_at	note
live_ledger_untouched: corpus/knowledge/obsidian-ledger.tsv stays header-only; the builder never writes it (test ledgers live under tests/vault/)

space_bearing_names.note: both basenames contain literal spaces; they are intentionally different names, so a tool that matches on basename instead of full path is caught

content.identical: cmp -s on the two files exits 0; both sha256sum values equal the constant

declared_ledger_rows.why: full match: both paths exist (literal spaces included) and both hashes are the actual file bytes

expect.why: byte-identical pair on both sides (space-bearing basenames) plus a fully matching ledger row (all four conjuncts)

accept.note: a harness may render the verdict as one token or as verdict+receipt fields; both satisfy this case as long as the verdict class is VERIFIED (never NOT-VERIFIED and never SAFE/NOT-SAFE r2 vocabulary) and the receipt, where printed, is moved-to-obsidian

failure_modes_caught: unquoted path handling: any component that word-splits or re-tokenizes the space-bearing path fails to find the file (or the ledger row) and reports NOT-VERIFIED
basename matching: the vault basename differs from the source basename, so a tool that matches on basename rather than the exact full path cannot receipt this pair
column splitting: a ledger parser that splits on runs of whitespace instead of tab breaks the path fields at the spaces, so the row never matches (the row's path fields contain literal spaces)
secret-shape false positive: neither path component matches the secrets-refusal shapes; a tool refusing this target for secret-shaped reasons is wrong

disarmed.method: run with a header-only ledger (e.g. `bash make-fixture.sh --ledger <tmp>/empty.tsv --skip-ledger`, then point the tool's ledger override at that file, or restore tests/vault/ledger-V8.tsv to header-only)
disarmed.why: the row is the receipt: without it the vault copy is not evidence

auxiliary_checks.why: byte-identical pair with space-bearing names but no ledger row: the row is the receipt, not the copy. Not listed in targets so runners evaluating the single-target contract are unaffected; exercised by selftest.sh.

crosscheck.note: the r2 tool tools/souji-verify.sh predates the r4 VERIFIED vocabulary; for these inputs its expected output is the same verdict pair under r2 names
crosscheck.expected_line: VERDICT	@FIXTURE_ROOT@/source/meeting notes 2026-10.md	SAFE	moved-to-obsidian	ledger-row vault=@FIXTURE_ROOT@/vault/Meeting Notes 2026-10.md source-sha256=2fc29f1f5638
crosscheck.seam: SOUJI_LEDGER env override (defaults to corpus/knowledge/obsidian-ledger.tsv, which stays header-only)

determinism.note: fixed content; two builds at different roots produce byte-identical files and equal sha256 values (paths vary per run); the builder asserts the constants and cross-checks this file

writes: <ROOT>/source/meeting notes 2026-10.md (0444 not required; vault side is 0444)
build.git: git init -q -b master on <ROOT> (offline, no commits) so the fixture root behaves like a real repo and the pushed receipt must fall through to the ledger
build.safety: never reads or writes the live ledger, the real vault, or any sibling repo; writes only under --out and --ledger FILE

notes: The builder writes ONLY: <FIXTURE_ROOT>/** and <LEDGER> (default tests/vault/ledger-V8.tsv). The live ledger and the real vault /home/vgpnk/Documents/shokoknowledge are never touched; this case is self-contained under tests/vault/.
The vault here is a fake vault dir under the fixture root — no Obsidian process, no CLI, no network is involved. /usr/bin/obsidian (the GUI launcher) is never executed by this case.
stdout contract: line 1 = JSON {case,root,targets,expect,vault,ledger,sha256}; line 2 = FIXTURE_READY V8 <absolute target path>; --quiet emits KEY=VALUE lines plus the FIXTURE_READY line.
Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 build/assertion failure, 2 usage.
Both target paths contain spaces: every consumer must quote them (including in the FIXTURE_READY line and in runner argv construction).
